SpaceX conducted its initial public offering on June 12, 2026, with a target valuation of US$1.77 trillion.
The company listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol SPCX.
Elon Musk retained 82–85% of the voting power post-IPO through his Class B super-voting shares.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley served as the lead underwriters for the SpaceX IPO.
JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Citigroup acted as other underwriters for the offering.
The IPO raised approximately US$86 billion for SpaceX's long-term ambitions including orbital AI infrastructure.
SpaceX acquired Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI in February 2026 at a valuation of $125 billion.
Nasdaq changed its rules to allow SpaceX early inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 index just 15 trading days after the IPO.
S&P Global reaffirmed that SpaceX would not be included in the S&P 500 index due to its net loss of $4.94 billion in 2025.
Anthropic signed a contract worth $1.25 billion per month with xAI to buy compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center.
Google signed a cloud computing agreement to pay $920 million monthly for compute capacity from SpaceX's Colossus infrastructure.
Bloomberg reported that underwriters denied subscription orders from investors in Hong Kong and China due to regulatory risks.
SpaceX launched a $20 billion bond issue ten days after its listing to repay bridge loan borrowings.
Analysts at 23 underwriting banks issued price targets ranging from $190 to $800 for SpaceX shares.
Professor Jay Ritter argued that the uniformity of analyst forecasts reflected copycat behavior rather than independent valuation work.
